title: schedule-state.json (the dedup state) has the same defect fixed for skipped-sessions.json: non-atomic write, silent reset on corrupt file, unlocked read-modify-write
evidence: recordScheduled uses plain writeFileSync; readScheduleState returns {} when JSON.parse fails or the body is not an object, so the next recordScheduled replaces the file with one row. Lost dedup keys can make a later tick schedule an already-scheduled session again (duplicate join). schedule-tick has no run lock, so overlapping ticks race. Data-write class.
fix_direction: Reuse the skipped-state pattern: temp+fsync+rename, acquireLock around read-modify-write, throw/quarantine on corrupt instead of {}, tick logs a WARNING and must not stop joining.
